questions: What heats the land at the start of the chain?
What happens to the air just above the warm land?
segments.say: The sun heats the land. Look at the rays pouring heat onto the land: the land warms the air above it, and that warm air begins to rise. Keep your student notes open at the weather, climate and sun definitions for this scene.

questions: What flows in when the warm air rises?
What do we call the moving air we feel?
segments.say: Warm air rises, cool air flows in. Watch the warm air climb while cooler air slides in to take its place - that moving air is what we feel as wind. Now try the rising-air questions on the worksheet in pairs.

questions: How do clouds form at the top of the chain?
Why can one cold day not tell us the climate is changing?
segments.say: Clouds gather, rain falls. High up the risen air cools into clouds and the heavy drops fall as rain, finishing the chain. Then take the exit ticket on your own - its first question revisits exactly the weather-versus-climate trap from this lesson.
segments.watchFor: A cold day today means the climate is getting colder. Listen and look for it in pair talk and on the exit ticket: One day of weather feels like the whole climate, so a single day is read as the trend. Send them back to the long pattern and to the correct turn: Today's weather is not the climate: climate is the pattern of weather over many years, not one cold or hot day.

title: Weather and climate: heat on the move
